evidence.positive: Against the running build (746a21c18, demo-demo tenant) the seeded SULFONAMIDE cross-reaction group was present in allergy_cross_reaction_groups with 9 RxNorm codes (9793,10180,10207,9524,10171,10173,10188,10169,10179) and SNOMED 387406002, mapped to medication category SULFONAMIDE; both demo SMX/TMP meds carried the tag; boot log read 'Imported 2 allergy cross reaction groups' for all four tenant schemas (mayo-mayo, mgb-mgh, mgb-icsnh identical: 9rx/1sn, mayo has 5 tagged meds). Created a patient + case via /api/admin/patients, added an allergy through POST /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/allergies with type=RXNORM identifier=9524 (sulfasalazine, deliberately NOT in master-rxnorm-list so only the new group can associate it), launched via POST /api/app-launch, then POST /api/cds/medication-selection for m-sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim-iv. Response contained ruleId a-general-allergy needsAction=true, title 'Allergy to Sulfamethoxazole-Trimethoprim', description 'Patient has allergy to SULFONAMIDE with reaction: Anaphylaxis. Consider alternative medication.', details.ALLERGY_ALLERGEN=SULFONAMIDE. Same result for m-sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim-oral, and for a second patient with type=SNOMED identifier=387406002. DB: patient_medication_allergies rows for both patients with medication_category_id -> SULFONAMIDE and null medication_id.
evidence.negative: Patient with an NSAID class allergy (SNOMED 372665008): selecting m-sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim-iv returned no a-general-allergy result and an empty fired list, while selecting m-ketorolac on the same patient fired a-general-allergy 'Patient has allergy to NSAID' (proves the rule path was live and the group boundary held). Patient with no allergy and patient with RxNorm 999999 (in no group and no rxnorm mapping): selecting SMX/TMP IV returned no a-general-allergy result and no patient_medication_allergies row was written.
evidence.red_check: Swapped the parent commit's (e47d305e6^) demo allergy-cross-reaction-groups.csv and master-medication-list.csv (0 SULFONAMIDE rows in each) into /app/resources/data/org/demo/... in the app container (md5 0c708e75... / 5fec851e...), restarted the container. Boot log then read 'Imported 1 allergy cross reaction groups' for demo-demo and the DB held only the NSAID group. Repeating the positive flow on fresh patients (RxNorm 9524 and SNOMED 387406002) selecting m-sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim-iv returned NO a-general-allergy result and no patient_medication_allergies row, while the NSAID control still fired for ketorolac. Restored the shipped CSVs (container md5 0ee7039e887cb0b23802de7b27dd1066 and c2ce0d68b126e2fbf095e6e939ec72fd, matching worktree HEAD), restarted, log read 'Imported 2 allergy cross reaction groups', DB showed NSAID+SULFONAMIDE, and the positive fired again with 'Patient has allergy to SULFONAMIDE'. The signature line occurs exactly once in the full container log, inside the red window.

caveats: Allergies were injected through the admin RXNORM/SNOMED allergy endpoint, which runs the same associateAllergiesViaRxNormMapping path as FHIR ingestion but bypasses the RXNORM_ALLERGY_MAPPING feature flag; the flag is seeded off with enabledTenants=[] in this build, so real EMR sulfa allergies only reach this group once a tenant is enabled (pre-existing OR-2791 behaviour, not changed by this ticket).
Selection was exercised on demo-demo only; mayo/mgb seeds were verified in the DB (same 9 RxNorm + 1 SNOMED codes, tagged meds present) but not driven through a medication selection.

The red check swapped resources rather than classes (the change is CSV-only); the pre-fix medication list did not strip the SULFONAMIDE tag from already-imported meds, so the red state removed the group but not the tag, which is what the association depends on.

Clinical completeness of the 9 RxNorm ingredients versus the DailyMed sulfonamide list in the ticket was not assessed; sulfamethoxazole (10180) alone already mapped directly via master-rxnorm-list before this change.

automation.assessment: Backend coverage of the mechanism is solid (MedicationAllergyRuleTest category match, AllergyAssociationServiceTest, AllergyCrossReactionGroupRepositoryTest). AllergyCrossReactionGroupCSVImporterTest pins the shipped demo CSV but only seeds the NSAID category, so the SULFONAMIDE rows are silently skipped there and nothing asserts the new group or the SULFONAMIDE tag on the SMX/TMP meds. qa-suite allergy.spec has no RxNorm/SNOMED cross-reaction scenario at all.
proposed_tests: AllergyCrossReactionGroupCSVImporterTest: seed SULFONAMIDE alongside NSAID and assert the demo file yields a SULFONAMIDE group with 9 RxNorm codes incl. 9524 and SNOMED 387406002, for all three org files.

Seed-consistency test (BundledAntibioticPathwayTest style): every master-medication-list row whose tags include SULFAMETHOXAZOLE_TRIMETHOPRIM* also carries SULFONAMIDE, and every cross-reaction group's category exists as a medication category in that org.
qa-suite ALG supplemental: RXNORM 9524 allergy -> select m-sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim-iv -> a-general-allergy fires with 'Patient has allergy to SULFONAMIDE'.
qa-suite ALG supplemental: SNOMED 387406002 allergy -> same medication -> a-general-allergy fires.
qa-suite ALG supplemental negative: NSAID SNOMED 372665008 allergy -> SMX/TMP IV selection yields no a-general-allergy while m-ketorolac does.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A sulfasalazine RxNorm allergy and a SNOMED sulfonamide class allergy each produced an a-general-allergy alert naming SULFONAMIDE when Sulfamethoxazole-Trimethoprim was selected.
Negative: An NSAID allergy, no allergy, and an unmapped RxNorm code produced no allergy alert for the same medication, while the NSAID control still fired for ketorolac.
Red check: Running the app on the pre-change CSVs imported only one cross-reaction group and the same sulfa allergies produced no alert, then the shipped files were restored and the alert returned.

Automation: Extend the importer test to the SULFONAMIDE group and add supplemental e2e scenarios for the RxNorm, SNOMED and NSAID-boundary cases.
